BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Seller Review: Project Kestrel – Departures from Buyer Playbook

Below is an issue-by-issue assessment of the Seller's draft positions. Each departs from the Buyer playbook in some material respect, and each must be corrected before Completion. I have grouped the most critical issues together, followed by secondary concerns.

---

## A. Material Departures Requiring Immediate Pushback

### 1. General Warranty Cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (unconditional)
**Seller position:** Aggregate liability capped at 20% of purchase price, unconditionally.
**Playbook position:** 25% starting position (AUD 6,000,000); 20% / AUD 4,800,000 is a conditional fallback **usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft**. No such authority has been granted.
**Why pushback:** This materially lowers the cap from our baseline and removes the buyer principal's gatekeeping function. Even if financials tighten, our default position cannot shift without explicit executive authorisation and identification of the competing draft. The Seller is simply proposing a cap that the Buyer cannot accept as drafted.
**Recommendation:** Restore the 25% starting cap. If negotiation ultimately requires the 20%, treat it as a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written sign-off and reference to the specific negotiated draft. Do not accept the Seller's unilateral proposal.

### 2. Thresholds: de minimis AUD 25,000 and a $250,000 excess-only basket
**Seller position:** Claim actionable only once de minimis of AUD 25,000 is exceeded and aggregate basket of AUD 250,000 is exceeded; seller liable only for the excess above the basket.
**Playbook position:** de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once the threshold is breached (standard "full liability up to basket" model).
**Why pushback:** Two problems. First, the Seller's de minimis threshold (AUD 25,000) is five times higher than ours (AUD 5,000), effectively insulating smaller claims from any payout. Second, the "excess only above basket" model is unusual and seller-favouring: it requires two separate thresholds to be crossed before the Seller discharges any liability whatsoever. Under our standard model, once the AUD 50,000 basket is breached, the Seller is liable for the full quantum of claims up to the cap (subject to the cap itself). The Seller's position effectively eliminates recovery on the majority of realistic warranty claims during the contemplated period.
**Recommendation:** Adopt the Buyer's standard thresholds. Require both the lower de minimis threshold and the basket to be specified explicitly, with the basket model matching the standard approach (seller liable for claims up to the basket amount once the de minimis threshold is met). Consider whether an additional basket for exclusion purposes (claims the Seller can avoid paying for by demonstrating they fall within known exceptions) is needed separately, but do not adopt the Seller's "excess only above basket" variant.

### 3. Time Limits: 18 months (unconditional)
**Seller position:** General warranty claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. Limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
**Playbook position:** 24 months baseline; 18 months is a fallback **needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given)**.
**Why pushback:** The Seller is adopting the shorter period unilaterally. A shorter claims window compresses the buyer's ability to investigate and respond. Because the threshold fallback was not approved, we cannot accept 18 months at this stage.
**Recommendation:** Confirm 24 months as the base claims period. If the parties agree to reduce to 18 months, that reduction requires Amelia Frost's prior written approval and must be expressly tied to that approval in the clause text. Do not accept the Seller's unconditional 18-month term.

### 4. Fundamental / Title Claims: merged into the general cap and time limit
**Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
**Playbook position:** Separate regime: 100% cap, minimum six years outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
**Why pushback:** Merging fundamental/title claims into the general regime destroys the distinct protective architecture designed to cover the most significant risks of the transaction. Title defects arising years post-Completion (and certainly beyond the general 18–24 month window) become unprotectable. A 100% cap across six years is essential for title, which is the single largest buyer risk.
**Recommendation:** Establish a separate paragraph (fundamental / title claims) with its own 100% cap and its own six-year period. Do not fold title into the general warranty clause.

### 5. Blanket Buyer-Knowledge Exclusion (Clause 8.3)
**Seller position:** "The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
**Playbook position:** Delete the blanket exclusion entirely. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; the exclusion must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Why pushback:** This is an absolute exclusion of claims based solely on the Buyer's own investigation. It leaves the Buyer without protection even for issues the Seller itself should have disclosed or discovered. This conflicts directly with Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct being carved out. With the fraud carve-out in place, knowledge exclusions that overlap with those carve-outs are doubly problematic because there is nothing left to excuse. More fundamentally, refusing to carve out fraud from a blanket knowledge rule creates a gap that could swallow fraud claims.
**Recommendation:** Delete Clause 8.3 entirely, or replace with a narrow provision limited to matters genuinely known to the Buyer through independent investigation with named knowledge sources. Ensure any residual exclusion explicitly carves fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out to the maximum extent enforceable.

### 6. Bluefen Change-Control Consent: "reasonable endeavours" treated as satisfied
**Seller position:** Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent using reasonable endeavours.
**Playbook position:** Require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied **before Completion**. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
**Why pushback:** The Seller's position treats a soft, achievable consent commitment as adequately satisfied. For a material customer change-control, "reasonable endeavours" does not satisfy our pre-Completion standard. Without evidence of satisfied conditions (including treatment rights, data migration plan, timeline, and related representations), the Buyer is exposed to operational disruption post-Close.
**Recommendation:** Replace with effective consent pre-Completion. Require specific representation and warranty evidence that associated conditions are satisfied, supported by substantive documents (change-control agreement, treatment rights documentation, data handling plan, transition timeline). Do not accept "reasonable endeavours."

### 7. Riverlark Facility Release: post-completion only
**Seller position:** A release to be provided following Completion; no immediate discharge.
**Playbook position:** Require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
**Why pushback:** A post-completion release of a ~AUD 3,200,000 bank facility creates significant financing and security exposure at Close. Our position demands that security be released *before* Completion funds are available, supported by an irrevocable undertaking that addresses the facility's outstanding balance and triggers. The Seller's "follow-on" approach gives the Buyer a lien or encumbrance risk until after Close.
**Recommendation:** Require (i) current payout from the facility outstanding, (ii) direct repayment sourced from Completion funds, (iii) a written irrevocable undertaking to release security, and (iv) approval by Amelia Frost for any post-Completion release. The irrevocable undertaking must identify the facility, the outstanding amount, and the repayment mechanism.

### 8. Employee Bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420,000 missing from funds flow
**Seller position:** Conditional bonuses recorded in DD-005 but not separately itemised in the Completion funds flow; funds flow does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
**Playbook position:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Why pushback:** Silent omission of a known contractual liability from the funds flow is a material breach of the completion mechanics. It could leave the Buyer underfunded at Close and raises questions about whether seller-funded assumption versus buyer-funded obligation. Additionally, unstated tax and on-cost exposure adds hidden cost.
**Recommendation:** Include DD-005 (AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs) as a specific line item in the Completion funds flow. State explicitly whether the Seller assumes this obligation; if not, identify who funds it. Disclose the tax, superannuation and on-cost treatment.

### 9. Title Evidence: DD-012 share register
**Seller position:** "Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012" recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%.
